title.narrative: OPC Serbia 2024-2027 Labour rights, decent work and social dialogue
OPC Serbien 2024-2027 Arbetarnas rättigheter, anständigt arbete, social dialog

description.narrative:
Olof Palme International Center (OPC) överlämnar till ambassaden ansökan om bidrag i Serbien för en period på 3 år och totalt 15 mSEK. OPC-applikationen kommer efter en öppen dialog med ambassaden och i förhållande till bidraget som startade 2016. och avslutades 2023.
Den långsiktiga utvecklingen förändras (påverkansnivå) som programmet syftar till uppmuntra är: Politiska och socioekonomiska processer i Serbien är transparenta och deltagande, vilket återspeglar rättigheter och intressen hos bemyndigade och organiserade medborgare som ställer pliktbärare till svars. Målet med programmet är att stärka kapaciteten och legitimiteten för civilsamhällets organisationer och stödverksamhet som säkerställer delaktigheten politiska, sociala och ekonomiska processer. Det civila samhällets organisationer kommer ge medborgarna möjlighet att hävda och utöva sina rättigheter och bidra till främjande av god förvaltning och socioekonomiska rättigheter.

The Olof Palme International Center (OPC) submits to the Embassy the application for a contribution in Serbia for the period of 3 years and total of 15 mSEK. The OPC application comes following an open dialog with the Embassy and in relation to the contribution that started in 2016. and completed in 2023.
The long­term development changes (impact level) that the programme aims to encourage is: Political and socio­economic processes in Serbia are transparent and participatory, reflecting the rights and interests of empowered and organized citizens that hold duty bearers accountable. The objective of the programme is to strengthen the capacity and legitimacy of civil society organisations and support activities that ensure the participatory nature of political, social and economic processes. Civil society organisations will empower citizens to claim and exercise their rights and contribute to the advancement of good governance and socio­ economic rights.

Some examples of results: Center for Democracy Foundation In the first project year, CDF made important progress in strengthening its institutional capacity, thematic focus, and partnerships, reinforcing its role as a credible civil society actor in the field of social and economic rights. Through its continuous engagement in the public policy debate, particularly in the areas of decent work, labour rights, and social protection, CDF enhanced its visibility and legitimacy among relevant stakeholders. CDF facilitated numerous public discussions and policy events involving MPs, trade unions, employers associations, and youth networks, effectively positioning itself as a platform for structured dialogue on social justice issues. These efforts contributed to building alliances with both formal and informal actors and strengthened CDFs role as an intermediary between citizens, institutions, and policy frameworks. Furthermore, CDF actively participated in programmelevel coordination and peer exchange, which added value to crosspartner learning and collective impact. CDF successfully informed citizens and civil society organisations about key reforms in social policy, labour rights, and Serbias EU accession process through a series of public events, publications, and media engagements. They also strengthened the capacities of CSOs, particularly in budget monitoring and labour law advocacy, and fostered structured participation in shaping policy recommendations and reform agendas. Through its policy research and public engagement activities, CDF continued to advocate for the implementation of European Pillar of Social Rights principles within Serbias labour and social protection frameworks. The organisation facilitated structured dialogues with parliamentarians, representatives of the Economic and Social Council, and other institutional stakeholders, providing concrete policy recommendations informed by its research and consultations
